title: Ayeuonganit Wampum Ayimꝏup
summary: Ayeuonganit Wampum Ayimꝏup, also known through Parrish Pond, is remembered by Shinnecock people as a wampum-making place. Shinnecock activists defended the land from subdivision in February 2000, and Southampton Town preserved part of the cultural landscape in 2014.
address_label: Parrish Pond / St. Andrews Circle area, Southampton (general)
map_geometry_source: Original On This Site Parrish Pond map location, checked against Southampton Town street mapping and preservation reporting.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Shinnecock Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The Parrish Pond struggle shows how Shinnecock cultural knowledge and direct action protected land threatened by development. Its history centers living Shinnecock stewardship and the cultural work of wampum-making rather than treating wampum only as an object of the past.
oral_history_content: Oral history of Parrish Pond by Shinnecock tribal member Daniel Collins. Audio courtesy Tomek Jeziorski, Adam Lenz, Shane Weeks & Karolina Zielińska. 1
history_content:
On February 24, 2000, Shinnecock activists and supporters gathered to oppose construction within the Parrish Pond subdivision. Rebecca Genia was among the Shinnecock land protectors arrested during two days of protest. Civil-rights organizer Bob Zellner was also arrested after arriving to help mediate. The related cases later ended in acquittal or dismissal.

The action challenged development in a landscape Shinnecock people identified as culturally significant for wampum-making. It also brought wider attention to the authority of Shinnecock knowledge when planning and preservation decisions affect ancestral land.

1
translation_content:
Shinnecock language contributor Tina Tarrant has translated Ayeuonganit Wampum Ayimꝏup as "in this place wampum was made." The name keeps the place connected with Shinnecock language, cultural memory, and wampum work.

1
preservation_content:
In 2014, Southampton Town approved the Community Preservation Fund purchase of 1.53 acres from Parrish Pond Associates. The purchase closed on November 18 for $908,014.11. Shinnecock advocates described the land as part of a wampum-making landscape and had worked for its protection since the 2000 protests.

1
excavation_content: Excavation of the Parrish Pond site was done in 1998 by Robert Kalin of the Archaeological SUS. Inc in Rocky Point, NY. According to the report, evidence of a camp, village, wampum workshop and other multi-component features were discovered on location.
